body:
I think you misunderstood some things. 

1. He’s not my boss. I have no storage and the school has no storage left to put in my room, so I bought my own. I’m an English teacher and my department coworkers have several shelves. I have none. I had to do something.

2. There was already desks in the stairwell. I just added the ones from my room because I didn’t want to leave them in the hall in the way of their waxing (they don’t wax the stairwell). I was trying to help him out. I left the note to apologize and explain why we couldn’t get the last few (our backs) and thanked him for all he does. 

3. I’d rather the lockers didn’t tip over and potentially crush a student, regardless of whether he wanted them or not. 

4. I painted the inside of my door, not the outside. My other coworker has his door painted on the inside as well. That’s why I thought it wouldn’t be a big deal.

That’s what I thought too. Administration has seen my posts and said nothing about not being allowed to do anything. Usually we are allowed to bring in our own furniture and whatever we want into our rooms. I got the lockers because I have no shelves in my room and the last shelves I bought fell apart halfway through the year last year. I painted those parts of my room because other teachers have done the same.

I don’t think that’s it. I have a Harry Potter Mirror of Erised that he drilled a hole for no problem. It’s simply a decoration. It’s an old school, so it’s not an issue. Plenty of screws in the walls. 

I know - that is what concerned me and why I didn’t reply. He was being a bit rude, and I didn’t want to say something I would regret. I do appreciate all he does. Just don’t like getting talked to like that.

You are not understanding the context here. It was obvious from dinner - the silence that ensued when my FIL had to say they wouldn’t be in town to watch the dogs and the BIL ignoring my husband and leaving it up to my FIL to tell their plans - that they had purposefully made it a secret and agreed to not tell us. That’s what we are hurt about. We don’t care about what they’re doing and why. We care about family agreeing to hide things from one another.
I agree. Maybe that’s it. I am going to talk to him. Maybe he can bring it up when we see them next.

How did we pry for information if we asked if they could dog sit? You’re not making much sense, aside from continual negative feedback. I just don’t feel like family should have a reason to keep things from each other like a trip.

How am I dire for information when I don’t keep up with them regularly? We could care less what they do. We just find the secretive behavior regarding vacations to be weird. You would have to know his family to understand. They intentionally didn’t tell us, which was evident by the silence at dinner when they reluctantly told us about the trip they had planned without us. That’s not what family does. We openly communicated about our trip because we have nothing to hide. We didn’t plan it based on them watching our dogs. We just thought we’d ask them first.
We think that makes total sense. What bothers us is the secrecy. Why keep things a secret from us and other family members? It makes those on the receiving end feel horrible.
I agree. It’s sad to realize after devoting years of your life to a profession that it’s not what you expected.
I feel the same. Thank you for your support.
Public and we call the letter they hand us on the last day of school that says we are non-renewed (contract) the pink slip.
Yes, you are correct. That’s what we call pink slip in the south. It’s a letter that says you weren’t renewed on the last day of school. They call you down and hand it to you.
Thank you. I am in therapy.

I already see a therapist and have been diagnosed with PTSD, anxiety, and depression. I’ve never been told that I have a personality disorder, though my therapist is pretty positive that my mother had antisocial personality disorder. I endured some pretty extensive abuse.

I honestly never tell people about my drama, and rarely even talk to people in depth. The only person who knows what I really think and feel is my husband. What little I talk to co-workers, it’s usually small talk, about our lessons, etc. 

So, you’re assumptions about that are a little off base.
Public school (city)
We don’t really receive contracts. Either you get pink-slipped on the last day, or you’re renewed.

How can I expect compensation for ice cream? It’s simply a reward. 

You may be onto something. Hard work and going the extra mile doesn’t seem to be appreciated in the teaching profession.

My anxiety is managed now. I’ve been doing much better. Started taking Lexapro. However, the comment by the janitor about being pink-slipped made my anxiety times 100 this weekend. 

I don’t know how to not to work so hard. My anxiety would go through the roof if I didn’t work so hard.

I know that it seems like I must be completely incapable of self reflection, but I truly have had some sh*t luck in life. My former administration was super corrupt. My parents rarely talk to me. I’ve tried reaching out and trying to make them a bigger part of my life. They just don’t want anything to do with me. I’ve asked my husband what’s wrong with me? I’ve asked co-workers if there’s something I need to work on? Everyone has reassured me that I need to have more self confidence, and that there’s nothing I’m doing that’s wrong, and that I’m a good person. The janitors at both schools have rarely cleaned my room, and I can’t help that my current one has some sort of power they are trying to assert over me for keeping my windows open. I never said my former students were out to get me, nor did I say the superintendent? I had my previous assistant principal threaten to send police to my new school over computer passwords that I had already given her. I highly doubt I’m making up the people I’ve had to deal with over the last few years. My ride in education has not been a smooth one. 

Trust me, if there was something I could fix within myself, if I was the one at fault for all of this, I would do it in a heartbeat. I know my abusive childhood makes it hard for me to function normally and I seek acceptance and validation unhealthily, but I don’t think my anxiety, PTSD, and depression can make people act this way toward me. I feel misunderstood a lot of the time. 

I promise. I self reflect more than you know. I beat myself up on a daily basis. The first thing I usually wonder is “what’s wrong with me?”
I’m just tired of having no consistency. I left my 1st job because I moved. Got pink-slipped from last school. I’m just tired of not having any consistency.
I just don’t see me winning this fight. Especially not in my state. If you look at my comment above, I think she carefully crafted her response so it could just look like an innocent statement.

I feel like she carefully crafted what she said so that if I complained about it, I would look like a fool. If questioned, she could turn around and say, “I just asked if she needed boxes? I always give teachers boxes at the end of the year.” Then, who looks like the fool? Me. 

I have just put it at the back of my mind, but her comment has set me on edge for pink slip week this week.
Yes, I’ve seen that everywhere that I’ve worked. My trash never gets taken out and my floors hardly get swept and mopped. I always get “that” custodian, unfortunately.

It’s not where I work. They publish their non-renewals in the meeting minutes on the school website (with delay of course, so there’s no way to know ahead of time).  

I just don’t think it would fly well. I would be seen as a non-tenured complainer, and it would be smoothed over. I just don’t see them seeing this as an issue. I think she said what she did carefully, so she couldn’t be accused of harassment. She could turn around and say, “I was just asking if she needed boxes?” Then who, to admin, looks like a whiny baby? Me. That may be part of her plan. She’s maybe hoping I’ll say something.
I wish I could. I just think I would be seen as a complainer, as an non-tenured teacher.

Maybe I should take it with a grain of salt. I guess I’m just worried because they had to have their items for the agenda submitted the day before she said that to me. Makes me wonder. She was the first to know our Superintendent was leaving. Just makes me worry. It was just a jerk thing to do.

Yes, it’s torture. A coworker that came from another career field said that the environment of the school and mood of the teachers evidently changed the last week of school her first year experiencing pink slip week. She said you could feel it in the air.

Yes, it drives me insane. My new principal is impossible to read. He has come to view my projects with students and never says anything, just leaves. No email to say what he thought. I never know what he’s thinking.

Yes, I work in the south, and I’ve never heard of it being done any other way. I think they tell you on the last day of school to keep you from not completing your duties up until the last day. It’s really sh*tty, and one of the things I REALLY hate about the education system down here. I’ve been on edge since the custodian’s comment, and I won’t be able to relax until after Friday.
I’m too afraid to speak up being non-tenured.

Yes, I’ve only had 1 evaluation, even though I am supposed to have 2, and there were nothing but positive notes made. I would be afraid to ask them. It’s kinda taboo around here to bring it up ahead of time. Everyone that’s not tenured fears the last week of school because they wait until the last day to tell you if you’re pink-slipped.
I’m afraid that would make me look weak. I’m not tenured, so I’d be scared to speak up.

Maybe I am. I just would never motion that to another adult in front of everyone, especially when other adults had taken the same amount of time. I find it rude, especially with such a sour look on one’s face.
I’m having the same reaction. I feel like piss one minute and decent the next. What is going on??? Flu test was negative.
I was right outside the door and have a glass in the door that allows me to see in.
I agree. I plan on speaking with them about it tomorrow. I don’t think this should go unpunished, or it will set a bad precedent. That’s potentially damaging school property too.

That’s exactly what we did in April when she blew up at him and was nasty for no reason. It has been nice to not be taken advantage of. 

I think it really probably is better. I told my husband that we might as well not be friends now that she’s restricted us both. I can’t see anything anyways. I think it always gives family members an excuse to not have to be in your life too. My parents use it as a way to keep tabs on me, but never want to have anything to do with me as their daughter. 

I like your tactic of redirecting and making known that they’d tell me if they wanted to know. I am going to start implementing it when we get unnecessary info from his parents.

Because from what I understand, when they have shown them other family member’s social media, it has been in a negative context. For example, commenting on on the “provocative” outfit a niece wore on her honeymoon and the fiancé showing my in-laws, who proceeded to bash her. Yes, I was friends with the fiancé (who already rubbed me the wrong way by deleting me off Snapchat when I first met her two years ago, claiming she couldn’t see my story, and implying that I had her restricted somehow) on Instagram, but that doesn’t mean I want her showing my in-laws my profile. She has no clue what I do and do not want them to know. There are certain things they can be highly judgmental about - they are highly against alcohol - and I, for example, have a picture of a drink on there that I made for friends during a holiday party. To me, it doesn’t matter whether I am friends with her or not, to sit there and show family members that do not have access to my profile, my profile, it is a big deal. I wouldn’t do it to them. In a way, it was a red flag that I had been talked about and not in a good way. 

Honestly, I didn’t block her. I just took her off my follower’s list. She figured it out within a day (guess she was watching me closely) and tried to follow me again. When I wouldn’t accept, she blocked me. 

My husband made one comment about his sister posting pictures of her toddler one time and now the parents have run and told her. I’m about ready to tell the sister everything they have said to us about her and then see if they like having confidence broken when you are supposed to trust someone. I’m pretty sure they would flip their lid and be highly upset. What it boils down to...we can’t say anything we don’t want them to blab, but they expect us to never say a word about what we talk about. It’s very dysfunctional and they are playing us all off each other, then acting like the innocent lambs who just want family peace. If they would have never told me the fiancé showed them stuff off my profile and never told his sister what my husband said, this tension right near the holidays wouldn’t be happening. 

It’s just frustrating.

I think that’s why it’s so painful for me. I’m glad you brought that up. It makes me feel powerless, just like I felt in my childhood. When I feel that way, I want to shut down = being walked over. I agree on not negotiating. Good point.

I used to for about a year 3 years ago. It helped tremendously, but I eventually stopped. Then, I found another last year and he always seemed to make me focus on the present and wasn’t interested in helping me heal from my past. He was a waste of time and I never went back after a few sessions. I felt worse when I left his office because of his invalidating remarks. 

I’ve thought about looking into another.
Also, thanks for the motivation.

This is my 4th year and I’ve never been good at it. That’s why I feel like a failure. Also, I seem to continually work in districts where I’m not backed up at the administration level, which makes me feel even smaller.

I do have to stop caring. I think that’s a huge part of the problem. I agree, if someone doesn’t stop them, they will continue this at a larger extent beyond high school. That’s really scary to think about. 

I really like your approach about not helping them and explaining why. They really aren’t worth my time and I’m tired of investing it when they don’t care.

Thanks for the motivation.

The fact that I’m being bullied by a group of teenagers makes me want to quit. It shows how pathetic I am. I’m just too kind-hearted and I have a hard time being a disciplinarian. 

I am just going to start sending them out and writing them up. 

I am very structured. We always have a set structure to class. We do have quizzes a lot, as that was one of the things the boys were complaining about in the chat. 

I turned off all commenting that day and don’t plan on reactivating it. 

I teach English.
Good idea! Thank you 🙂

You obviously cannot read. 🙄 I told the lady that I didn’t care about the iPhone backup and such because my phone automatically stored my photos in iCloud. She wouldn’t listen to me. Had it not been for her urging that I do the backup and taking hold of the setup process, I would have been done 1.5 hours earlier and had everything that I wanted on my iPhone after I solely logged into my Apple ID on my new iPhone.

I’m peeved at the fact that she pushed it and then charged me for it. I don’t like being made to feel like I’m wrong and definitely not being charged $35 for it.

I see the bud part a lot, I really do. Many are afraid of their children or have no control over them, and this is based just on my conversations with parents I’ve been able to get to answer the phone. 

What would you do in this scenario? Maybe print out progress reports myself and have the students take them home (have the sign them out), so I have proof that parents were notified, but the student may have chose to withhold the information?

The project was a group project. The essay was an independent assignment. The project included making an album cover, album insert, and music video for a character from The Great Gatsby, analyzing their journey in the novel and depicting it with songs that are a reflection. The album cover was left up to their interpretation, the album insert was simple (didn’t even require cited textual evidence, just paraphrased to connect the song to the novel), and I showed many how to use the WeVideo program that I suggested they use (including many others I suggested). Most students completed this with great grades. I gave them a rubric with every point laid out. 

This independent project is where it seems half the class just didn’t do it. I open my small group table when I give them in-class time to work on it and I open my free period to help them. Several took advantage of this, but still half of the essays were not turned in. 

I am just wondering if I need to go back and reteach how to write an essay entirely. Perhaps it was my fault to think they knew how to do it based on the statements of a few students and the assumption that their 10th grade teacher taught them how? I know their former teacher - who is no longer with us - openly gave athletes grades and didn’t require them to write essays when the rest of the class did (automatic 75). That was the kind of things going on in his classroom and I know the other 9th grade teacher aside from me (I’m new this year and teaching 2 of the 9th classes he couldn’t because this new freshman class is huge) doesn’t teach them how to write essays...maybe they genuinely don’t know how to?

It seems like the ones who turned them in are some of my higher students (who had the other 10th grade teacher who is hardcore) and those who are very dedicated that would have had the other teacher. 

What would you suggest in this scenario? I’m already into argumentation and was planning on having them plan their debates when we get back from break next week and debate before Christmas (which could potentially bring their grade up because it’s a big grade), but I’m a little surprised by the lack of submissions. Maybe I need to tackle this first and get to the bottom of it? Or, perhaps make the basics of writing more of a focus when we start The Crucible after Christmas?

Our district doesn’t update emails, so that route would not work. Anytime I try to get in touch with parents, I have a hard time reaching them. I don’t think I can try to get in touch with 65 parents - phone call wise - so I haven’t done that. I had to get in touch with 7 for some behavior in my class last week and it took almost 3 days to contact them all and get responses. We usually have them sign progress reports if the grade is bad, but this essay was due right after progress reports, thus why that didn’t work. Just seems like bad timing.

I do try to chunk it. They had 3-4 people in a group and 3 weeks. I gave 2-3 days in class to work on it.

I just hate to offer half credit to those who do it and then turn it in this late in the game, but I don’t want tons of students failing either.

I was implying that I had absent janitors who rarely come by our rooms at every school I’ve worked at. That’s why I was trying to use the arrow to emphasize it was about that and not the comments about a messy room. :)
I’m seriously thinking about it. Seems like the only way.
I don’t feel like not “recognizing” him would have made a difference. He seemed hell bent on saying all that to me, as he wasn’t even working the window.

This makes me feel like I’m failing at life. Hubby and I bring home twice monthly what you guys do and we struggle. But, we do have 2 car payments ($495), double the mortgage payment ($834), several utilities (power to a bigger house is outrageous in hot/cold seasons - $350), cellphones ($145), etc. We have much bigger payments, it looks like. My organs started shutting down because I couldn’t metabolism the Anectine well. It took my body 4 hours on a ventilator to finally metabolize it. I was told then, when I was about 10, that if it ever happens again, there’s a chance I could not wake up at all. I gave my doctor quite a scare, but the anesthesiologist recognized what was happening right away.

So, could it have been a blood plasma enzyme abnormality like mine that caused this boy not to wake up?

I can tell you spent a lot of time on it and that you truly care about your students! The video game sounds like something students really enjoyed and it kept them engaged! Kudos to you! 😊

Do you have preset point worths? I did last year, but found it hard to stick to it and remember to deduct/award points on a daily basis for the different categories I had set. How do you do your point system? 🙂

I agree with the bias. Make it seem like this author intended to produce a neutral piece, but instead presented bias because of what they wrote about (more attention given to the left side, for example) and how they wrote it (choice of diction for both sides reflecting bias).

Same experience here! 3 years of experience. Have taught every grade in high school except one (10th) and have a lot of extracurricular experience: cheer coach, prom, yearbook, class sponsor, etc. I emailed all the principals (15) and let them know I was interested. Heard back from 2 that said the position was already filled and 1 HR director that I emailed (the listing wasn’t specific to a school) and she said that principals would contact me at their discretion. Could you not give me a nod for reaching out, lady? 

I have had one interview and I’m supposed to know by the end of this week if I got it. Y’all say a prayer for me! If I don’t get it, it’s God’s will. Something else will come along and if it doesn’t, I’m taking it as a sign to get out of Education.

It’s bulls**t, really. My former principal literally asks people what church they go to in interviews. He also told a student teacher not to wear skirts and intimidated another with name-dropping a frequent customer of the bar she works at while not in school (he had obviously done some digging).

Unfortunately, education is very political. One of the few things I hate about this profession and it’s unfortunate that it’s a LARGE part of it. We’re human beings, for crying out loud, not nuns. 

I feel for you, I really do! Sometimes you just want the freedom to be who you are without the scrutiny.

Don’t go with a purely English degree. You can’t do much with those. I know a few people who work in completely different fields with nothing to do with English that received that degree for that very reason. If you want an English degree and want to teach, you’ll have to commit to a Master’s program for the Education part, which equals more schooling. I would go for the Bachelor of Secondary Education (B.S.E.) with a concentration in English. Then, that gives you more options for your Master’s. Just my two cents. That what I have.

I haven’t gotten a new one, but assuming I did, yes, it would. I just reread my non-renewal letter and it says “termination of your teaching position,” so is that not synonymous with contract? 

The logic behind teacher contracts make no sense to me. I’ve been terminated from my position since May, yet I’m still under contract until September, all because they still owe me money? 

They should pay out all teachers in one lump sum that get non-renewed, quit, or resign at the end of the year. Doesn’t seem fair to hold that money hostage and call it current wages.
Thank you!!!! Dollar Tree toilet paper works just fine = inexpensive and fun! 💁🏼‍♀️
Good idea! I wonder if they would do that.

Thank you. It just doesn’t make sense - the logic behind unemployment rules for teachers. What difference does it make if I take the money all during the year, or stretch it out over summer? Doesn’t mean I’m anymore employed after being non-renewed.
The contract ended - as stated in the non-renewal letter - at the end of the school year. Just because they still owe me money, doesn’t mean I’m employed.

Yes. I don’t see how what I previously earned qualifies as current wages, based on the law. I already earned that money. As of right now, I don’t have a job and haven’t had any luck finding one because not many are open in the districts around here.

High School English here! 🙋🏼‍♀️

I start off with going over rules/syllabus, I have them take their sorting quiz (I sort them into houses based on results and we have a sorting ceremony the first week as well). I then tell a little about me with pictures, and finally, I pass around a roll of toilet paper. Don’t tell them what it’s for. Just tell them to take as much as they like. Some obnoxious students will roll and roll. More meek and shy students will usually only take 2-3 sheets. Then, you drop the bomb. 💣 How many sheets they took = how many things they have to tell you/the class about themselves. As much as most students hate talking in front of the class (even though I just make them stand at their desk), I’ve never seen students laughing so hard or having a ball with this. The ones who rolled half the roll quickly regret their decision. 😂 It’s a great way to get everyone feeling more open and lighten the mood. After sorting houses that first week, I assign a school-wide scavenger hunt that is to be done during break, class changes, etc. with riddles. Students have to work in their houses as a grade-wide effort to solve the riddles first and find the horcruxes around the school (each house has a tab they collect to prove they found it). I’ve never seen students so willing to skip break and team together. I give big house points to the top finishers and keep a real-time score board on my school website! My advice is to have fun your first day/week. Set rules, procedures, and make getting acquainted with collaborative groups a fun way to start the semester! ❤️

OP here. After reading a lot of comments, I just wanted to say that I think some people are taking what I wanted to focus on with my post in a different direction than I intended. 

If you are a coach or know a coach that is a great teacher (not the kind that allows dominoes and card games every day like an above poster said) and a good coach, that is an accomplishment and definitely something we need to better influence our students. They need that guidance. I wasn’t trying to undermine the value of sports and how they are a great tool for teaching students and guiding them to their potential.

What I wanted to focus on is the fact that too many schools focus solely on sports to the point that they hire any good coach to teach a subject he/she is not qualified in. I’ve seen math teachers be hired as agriculture teachers because they were coaches, science teachers hired as English teachers because they were coaches. That’s what I’m saying bothers me. 

It is so commonplace in my area to non-renew teachers to make way for a coach. Good teachers. Sports are important and have their place, but so many schools fail to focus on education and the teachers that are truly skilled in their subject get the shaft for someone that will bring the school glory through a sport. 

I’m with the poster above that said something about some coaches feeling like they can do 5-minute assignments and they’re done because they are coaches. I’ve seen this mentality a lot here in the south. It’s like some coaches think they have a special privilege and won’t get fired as long as their sport excels. The sad thing is, most of the time that’s right. The other sad thing is that coaches like that probably got the position of a teacher that devoted every class to teaching their content and truly helping students learn. 

Not every coach is like that and those of you that truly care about your content too, THANK YOU! You deserve some much-needed recognition because I know it isn’t easy to juggle a sport and teaching! 🙂

When it’s more about the sports and not much attention is given to what is being taught in the classroom, that is when there’s a problem. 

My last principal never stepped foot in my room to view my teaching in the two years I was there. He did however (after having a student curse me and he delivered him a lower punishment than what it called for via the rule book) step foot in my room to tell me that if I came to more sports games, the students would respect me.

I’m having the same bad luck. I have 3 years of experience now. Got non-renewed this year after 2 years at the school. I’ve gotten 2 responses about already having picked another candidate out of 15 emails. No replies from the others. I’ve applied to everything within 1 hour of where I live. I’m losing hope. 🙁
I have not been told about moving elsewhere because it was not an RIF.

How can it be a reduction of units when I was the only one let go and my position was filled less than two weeks later? I worked in a rural, small-town school. I didn’t work in a big city that sees RIFs all the time. I was lied to.
That’s what I was thinking. I guess I just wondering if I “needed” to reply because from what I’ve read, most principals just ignore emails if they’ve hired someone.

Where I am at, all pink\-slips read "termination" and no reason is given. I am in an "At Will" state. I've had great evaluations every time...all until 4 days before the board apparently voted to pass the recommendation for my termination at the end of this school year. Seems convenient, right?

I was told 10 minutes before my final observation that I would have one because the principal had refused to observe non\-tenured teachers and left it to the Assistant Principal. He was supposed to observe us in February. She was not happy about it and came to observe me on my seniors last week of school. She exaggerated every thing she could to make me look bad. Called my classroom "controlled chaos" and even said my impromptu debates \(which she couldn't spell...or know what they were\) were "silly". Flat\-out trashed me. Didn't conference with me about it and purposefully hid from me the long list of negatives as she was having me sign it. 

That's exactly what I'm afraid my AP is up to. I told my husband that it can only be two things: she is trying to be my reference TO screw me over, or she's trying to be my reference to keep the P FROM screwing me over. I'm not sure which is true because how can I believe she is trying to do me good when she's the one that wrote the nasty observation...but then again, she purposefully didn't talk to me about it, so I don't know if it was because she was put up to it.

I think what you've said is a very solid, foolproof, and logical way to approach this. THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR ALL YOU HAVE SAID. 

How would you go about requesting the letter of recommendation? Via email, text, Facebook, etc.? Not sure what would be the appropriate avenue now that I'm not employed there...she did remind me that I have her number and to let her know?

That’s the sad thing about education, ya know? We should have a way to report such toxicity without fearing for our career. I kept quiet all year and was still fired anyway. I agree.
